# ANOMALY REPORT — a standing year-over-year sweep of every Cedar Press collection

*Generated by `code/227_anomaly_sweep.py` on 2026-08-26T19:44:24-04:00 in 328s. **Do not hand-edit — re-run the script.***

Every figure below is computed from the file named beside it, at the mtime stamped in §Sources. Several agents write these files concurrently; **a count without a vintage is a claim about a file that no longer exists.**

---

## What this document is

> Elijah, 2026-08-26: *"For all the datasets, do an analysis if there is anything odd — because we have year-to-year data over such a long time horizon, that allows us to do good sanity checks. Like, did an entity suddenly get a bunch of money one year? Is that explainable?"*
>
> And, the same day: *"Also do research to make sure it's not like data coverage or reporting impacting coverage as well — we need to be clear what the assumptions and limitations of the datasets are."*

**A spike is either a fact about the world, a fact about the rules, or a fact about our pipeline.** Year-over-year is how you tell them apart. Every anomaly here is typed as exactly one of four things.

| type | meaning |
|---|---|
| `PIPELINE` | Our code, our pull, our linkage. An artefact we made. It has an owning script. |
| `REGIME` | **A reporting rule changed.** A threshold moved, a filing frequency doubled, a relief programme opened. The step is a fact about a statute — not about Indian Country, and not about our code. |
| `WORLD` | A fact about the world that survived both of the above. |
| `UNKNOWN` | We could not separate the candidates. **Named, with every candidate stated, never smoothed over.** |

**ORDER OF INFERENCE: PIPELINE first, then REGIME, then WORLD.** `WORLD` is the hardest verdict to earn, not the default when nothing else is obvious. Mis-typing a regime step as WORLD is how a publication ships a confident sentence about tribal economies that is really a sentence about a statute. Where a regime change and a real effect are confounded and cannot be separated, the row is `UNKNOWN` **with both candidates named** — we do not pick the more interesting one.

**An unexplained spike that ships is how a publication gets embarrassed; an explained one is often the story.**

`docs/anomaly_report.json` is the diffable artefact and is the point of making this standing rather than a one-off. Re-run after any build and diff the JSON: an anomaly that **changes type**, or a **new seam appearing**, is a regression in the data even when every build succeeded.

### Read alongside

- `docs/ASSUMPTIONS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md` — a concurrent agent owns the dated register of reporting regimes. Every `REGIME` row below names the event key it matched (`COVID_RELIEF`, `HLOGA_QUARTERLY`, …) so the two documents can be reconciled row by row.
- `data/clean/series_breaks.csv` — the per-column break register this sweep is the detector for.
- `docs/DATA_ODDITIES.md` — what a zero, a negative and a blank mean per dataset.
- `docs/CICD_BENCHMARK.md` — the external reconciliation. `INTERNAL-05` there and the seam section here are the same defect seen from two directions.

## THE TEN THAT WOULD MOST EMBARRASS A PUBLICATION

*`PIPELINE` or `UNKNOWN` only — a figure that is wrong about our own data rather than merely surprising about the world. A `REGIME` row is a caveat you must print; one of these is a number you must not print at all. Ranked by severity then dollars, then capped at three per class and three per dataset so that one defect cannot own the list.*

### 1. `PIPELINE` · `ID_SCHEME_SEAM` · federal_funding_transactions.tribe_id: 2 IDENTIFIER SCHEMES in one column, switching at 2007/2008, 2022/2023

`AN-b2b0c3b67910` — a content-addressed id, stable across runs; diff on it.

**$107.50B at stake.** 549,530 rows.

- PIPELINE candidate: The entity column 'tribe_id' holds MORE THAN ONE IDENTIFIER SCHEME (INTEGER, NEID) and which one a row carries depends on WHICH YEAR it is from. Nothing is blank and nothing is malformed - the same entity simply has two ids.
- PIPELINE boundary 2023-2023 (115_pull_assistance_archive.py + 24_funding_merge.py): FY2023 IS THE ONLY YEAR SERVED BY BOTH ERAS - 34,511 rows from the FY2023 archive zip and 15,141 from the 2023-04-09 do-file extract. It therefore carries BOTH identifier schemes at once (see ID_SCHEME_SEAM), which inflates any distinct-entity count for that year specifically.
- rows per scheme: INTEGER=365,535, NEID=178,820, OTHER=5,175
- dollars per scheme: INTEGER=$107.50B, NEID=$59.78B, OTHER=$1.36B
- era map (year: modal scheme, printed only where it changes): 2007: NEID | 2008: INTEGER | 2023: NEID
- 29 canonical names appear under BOTH schemes - each of those is ONE entity counted as TWO. The true overlap is larger, because the two eras also render the same name differently and only exact matches are counted here.
- CONSEQUENCE, and it is the publishable-number kind: **a per-entity total on this column SPLITS an entity at the boundary**, and **a distinct-entity count DOUBLE-COUNTS every entity present in both eras**. Neither failure looks wrong: the totals still add up and every row still has an id.
- TO FIX: a crosswalk applied at build so one column carries one scheme, or a second normalised column. Check whether a `*_neid` column already exists and is POPULATED on the legacy rows - on the assistance table it exists and is populated on ZERO of them, so the crosswalk is absent, not merely unused.

## SEAMS — the class that masquerades as a finding

*A seam is a column whose meaning changes at a boundary in OUR pipeline rather than at a plausible real-world date. It is the single most dangerous class in this repo, because a filter on a seamed column returns a clean, plausible, wrong answer, and nothing about the output looks broken.*

**27 NEW seam candidates. 1 known seams re-detected (regression check passing — the detector still sees them).**

<details><summary><code>REGIME</code> native_entity_lobbying_disclosures.dt_posted: day-of-month clusters on day 20 (4,706), day 19 (2,319)</summary>

- expected ~927 per day over 27,796 dated rows if days were uniform
- day-of-month counts: day 20=4,706, day 19=2,319
- THE LDA FILING DEADLINE, NOT FALSE PRECISION. Quarterly LD-2 reports are due on the 20th of January, April, July and October, and the day-20 pile-up is filers meeting it. Note this is the SAME statute (HLOGA, 2008) that doubled filing frequency - so the deadline structure itself changes mid-panel.
- Whatever the cause, the remedy is a PRECISION FIELD beside the date, never a corrected date. A date silently promoted to day-precision cannot be un-promoted.

</details>

<details><summary><code>UNKNOWN</code> native_entity_lobbying_disclosures.spend_usd: first-digit distribution departs from Benford (chi2 1,881 on 16,492 positive values; digit 2 at 25.3% against 17.6% expected)</summary>

- observed first-digit shares: 1:22.9%, 2:25.3%, 3:15.5%, 4:10.9%, 5:8.7%, 6:9.3%, 7:2.2%, 8:2.8%, 9:2.4%
- WHAT THIS CAN SHOW: that the digit distribution is not what an unconstrained multiplicative process produces. WHAT IT CANNOT SHOW: fabrication. Federal money is FULL of legitimate reasons to fail Benford - appropriations are round, programmes have caps and floors, awards are negotiated to round figures, and formula grants are computed from populations. A Benford failure here is a PROMPT TO LOOK, never a finding on its own, and it must never be published as evidence of anything.

</details>

## THE REGIME REGISTER — reporting rules that move this data

*Checked before any step is called a fact about the world. This register is the reason `WORLD` is hard to earn here. A concurrent agent owns `docs/ASSUMPTIONS_AND_LIMITATIONS.md`; these keys are how the two documents line up.*

| key | years | datasets | may explain | what changed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `COVID_RELIEF` | 2020–2021 | `federal_funding_transactions`, `np_financials`, `np_schedule_i_grants`, `grantmaker_funding_flows`, `prime_contracts`, `subawards` | *all* | CARES Act (2020) and ARPA (2021) sent unprecedented direct funding to tribal governments - reportedly ~$8B and ~$20B. THE SINGLE BIGGEST CONFOUNDER IN THIS PANEL. Any 2020-2021 assistance spike is presumptively REGIME until the programme mix is shown to be ordinary. |
| `ARRA` | 2009–2011 | `federal_funding_transactions`, `prime_contracts`, `np_financials`, `faads_entity_attribution` | *all* | American Recovery and Reinvestment Act. Same shape as COVID relief, smaller, inflating 2009-2011. |
| `HLOGA_QUARTERLY` | 2008–2008 | `native_entity_lobbying_disclosures`, `tribe_year_lobbying_panel` | `ENTITY_APPEARANCE`, `ENTITY_SPIKE`, `VOCABULARY_SEAM`, `YEAR_STEP_ROWS` | LDA filing frequency went SEMIANNUAL to QUARTERLY under HLOGA, effective 2008. This roughly DOUBLES filing counts with no change in lobbying activity. ANY FILING-COUNT TREND CROSSING 2008 IS CORRUPTED unless it is computed on dollars or on filings-per-reporting-period. |
| `FFATA_SUBAWARD` | 2010–2012 | `subawards` | *all* | FSRS/FFATA subaward reporting began 2010 with a $25,000,000 prime threshold lowered to $25,000 in October 2010. Counts rise 30 -> 113 -> 1,652 -> 2,679 across FY2009-12. That is the threshold, not the activity. Subawards below the threshold are absent BY RULE. FY2012 forward is the first comparable stretch. |
| `NAGPRA_2024_RULE` | 2024–2026 | `nagpra_notices` | *all* | NAGPRA's revised regulations (43 CFR 10) took effect January 2024 and changed notice requirements. A surge in notices after that date is regulatory before it is discovery. Establish how much is the rule before calling any of it a change in institutional behaviour. |
| `DUNS_TO_UEI` | 2022–2022 | `prime_contracts`, `federal_funding_transactions`, `subawards` | `DUPLICATE_KEY`, `ENTITY_APPEARANCE`, `ENTITY_DISAPPEARANCE`, `VOCABULARY_SEAM` | The federal government retired DUNS and adopted the UEI on 2022-04-04. An identifier discontinuity mid-panel: an entity has DUNS-keyed history and UEI-keyed history that do not join without a crosswalk. |
| `CFDA_TO_ASSISTANCE_LISTINGS` | 2018–2018 | `federal_funding_transactions` | `VOCABULARY_SEAM` | CFDA was renamed Assistance Listings and moved to SAM.gov in 2018. Numbers largely persisted; programme titles and groupings did not. Join on the number, never the title. |
| `NAICS_REVISIONS` | 2002, 2007, 2012, 2017, 2022 | `prime_contracts`, `subawards` | `VOCABULARY_SEAM` | NAICS is revised every five years (2002/2007/2012/2017/2022): codes added, retired, split, merged. An industry series across a revision year compares different definitions. |
| `IGRA_ERA` | 1988–1995 | `gaming_facility_metrics`, `gaming_facilities` | *all* | IGRA (1988) and the first compacts created the reporting universe itself. Early-1990s growth is an institution being built, not a market expanding within a stable one. |
| `ROLLCALL_SOURCE_FLOOR` | 1989–1990 | `_bill_actions`, `bill_votes` | *all* | House EVS begins at calendar 1990 and Senate LIS at the 101st Congress. Pre-1990 vote metadata comes from ICPSR descriptions and is not comparable to post-1990. |
| `SETASIDE_TIER_2013` | 2013–2016 | `prime_contracts` | *all* | DOI's 2013 Buy Indian rule created a SECOND TIER of Native set-aside. `Indian Business` is zero in every year FY2000-2013 and then overtakes `Buy Indian`. READ ALONE, `Buy Indian` SAYS NATIVE SET-ASIDES FELL 62%; SUMMED, THEY ROSE 44%. The whole difference is one code appearing. Always sum the family; never trend a single set-aside code across 2013-2016. |
| `IHS_BUY_INDIAN_2022` | 2022–2022 | `prime_contracts` | *all* | IHS did not adopt the two-tier Buy Indian architecture until 2022-03-14. Pooling agencies therefore puts a SECOND false break in the set-aside series, at a different date from DOI's. An agency-pooled Native set-aside trend crosses both. |
| `FAR_4606_MICRO_MODIFICATIONS` | 2000–2026 | `prime_contracts` | **context only — never types a row** | STANDING LIMITATION (never types a row). FAR 4.606(a)(1) requires modifications to be reported REGARDLESS OF DOLLAR VALUE, so the row count is a count of ADMINISTRATIVE ACTIONS, not of contracts or of money. Measured on FY2026: **71.9% of rows with a positive obligation are <=$2,500, median $443.** A contract-COUNT trend running into FY2026 is an artefact of reporting practice. Count awards (a de-duplicated PIID key), or report dollars. |
| `SINGLE_AUDIT_THRESHOLD` | 2004–2015 | `fac_tribal_single_audits` | **context only — never types a row** | STANDING LIMITATION (never types a row). The Single Audit threshold moved $300k -> $500k -> $750k. An entity below the threshold has NO AUDIT BY RULE. Absence from this layer is never evidence of absence of federal money. |
| `ACQUISITION_THRESHOLDS` | 2000–2026 | `prime_contracts` | **context only — never types a row** | STANDING LIMITATION (never types a row). Micro-purchase and simplified-acquisition thresholds moved repeatedly across this window. A change in the COUNT of small contracts may be a threshold change rather than a change in contracting behaviour - but the window is the whole panel, so it can never explain ONE year, and a register entry that explains every year explains none. |
| `FORM_990N` | 2008–2026 | `np_financials`, `np_orgs` | **context only — never types a row** | STANDING LIMITATION (never types a row). 990-N (e-Postcard) filers report no financial detail: 6,453 of 12,764 organisations. A zero in a revenue column there is the FILING REGIME, not a finding about the organisation. |
| `SECTION_7871` | 1996–2026 | `np_schedule_i_grants`, `grantmaker_funding_flows` | **context only — never types a row** | STANDING LIMITATION (never types a row). Under IRC section 7871 tribal governments are not 501(c)(3) and file no Form 990. This is the likely mechanism behind Schedule I recipient EINs absent from the BMF - the recipient is real and the filing does not exist. |

### REGIME STRESS TESTS — the register is only worth having if it is testable

*Naming a rule change beside a step is a hypothesis. Measuring whether the step survives an instrument the rule change cannot touch is a result. Both tests below re-run every sweep and both are built to be able to come back the other way — a stress test that can only confirm is not a test.*

#### `RS-01` · `HLOGA_QUARTERLY` — **TREND SURVIVES**

*Does the fall in lobbying-registrant concentration survive the 2008 semiannual-to-quarterly filing change?*

Measured on `data/clean/native_entity_lobbying_disclosures.csv`, mtime 2026-08-06T16:19:37.

- THE DOUBLING IS REAL AND IT IS FILINGS ONLY. Filings go 712 (2007) -> 1,344 (2008), x1.89 - almost exactly the semiannual-to-quarterly factor of 2. Over the same boundary the number of DISTINCT REGISTRANTS goes 135 -> 127, x0.94. More paperwork, the same people. Any 'lobbying activity rose' claim built on filing counts across 2008 is measuring HLOGA.
- THE CONCENTRATION TREND SURVIVES THE BREAK. Top-5 registrant share measured on FILINGS falls 28.8% (1999-2003 mean) -> 23.4% (2021-25 mean). Measured on DOLLARS - an instrument HLOGA cannot touch, because a share is scale-free and the same money is reported either way - it falls 54.5% -> 32.9%, a LARGER decline. **The finding is not an artefact of the filing-frequency change.**
- TWO CAVEATS THAT STILL TRAVEL WITH IT. (1) The dollar series is volatile in 1999-2003, where annual filings are 397-578 against ~1,200 later, so the early level is a small-N estimate. (2) Report PERIOD length changed at the same date, so per-FILING dollars are not comparable across 2008 even though annual totals and shares are. Quote the share, never the per-filing average.

#### `RS-02` · `COVID_RELIEF` — **SPIKE IS THE STATUTE**

*How much of the FY2020-21 assistance spike is COVID relief, measured on dollars rather than row counts?*

Measured on `data/clean/federal_funding_transactions.csv`, mtime 2026-08-26T18:12:57.

- FY2020: $20.59B against an FY2017-19 mean of $9.56B, an excess of $11.03B. Named COVID relief listings alone account for $7.47B - **67.7% of the entire excess**. Largest single mover: 21.019 'CORONAVIRUS RELIEF FUND' at $7.47B.
- FY2021: $40.80B against an FY2017-19 mean of $9.56B, an excess of $31.24B. Named COVID relief listings alone account for $22.07B - **70.7% of the entire excess**. Largest single mover: 21.027 'CORONAVIRUS STATE AND LOCAL FISCAL RECOVERY FUNDS' at $20.23B.
- THE FIGURES CORROBORATE THE PUBLISHED ONES. The reported ~$8B (CARES) and ~$20B (ARPA) to tribal governments land on CFDA 21.019 Coronavirus Relief Fund and CFDA 21.027 Coronavirus State and Local Fiscal Recovery Funds in this table at close to those magnitudes. Two independent routes to the same number is the strongest evidence available that the spike is the statute.
- AND THE ROW COUNTS WOULD HAVE HIDDEN IT. Assistance rows move 49,195 (FY2020) -> 48,415 (FY2021) - essentially flat, and FY2021 is LOWER - while dollars go $20.59B -> $40.80B. **Relief arrived as a small number of very large transactions.** Anyone sanity-checking this panel on row counts alone would have concluded nothing happened in 2021.
- FY2024 IS THE ONE TO WATCH, AND IT IS NOT COVID. FY2024 runs $16.24B against the same baseline, and its top movers are IHS self-governance, Indian Housing Block Grants, Section 8 vouchers, Highway Planning and Grid Infrastructure Deployment - an infrastructure-era composition, not a relief one. That elevation is a CANDIDATE real finding rather than a regime artefact, and it is where the reporting effort should go.

#### `RS-03` · `FAR_4606_MICRO_MODIFICATIONS` — **ROW COUNTS ARE NOT CONTRACT COUNTS**

*Is a prime-contract row count a count of contracts, or a count of administrative modifications?*

Measured on `data/clean/prime_contracts.csv`, mtime 2026-08-26T18:45:37.

- FY2026: **71.9% of rows with a POSITIVE obligation are $2,500 or less**, median $443. FAR 4.606(a)(1) requires modifications to be reported REGARDLESS OF DOLLAR VALUE, so a row in this table is an ADMINISTRATIVE ACTION, not a contract and not a unit of money.
- AND IT IS NOT CONSTANT ACROSS THE PANEL, WHICH IS WHAT MAKES IT A TREND-KILLER. The same share reads 3.0% in FY2000. Series: 2000=3.0%, 2001=4.5%, 2002=6.4%, 2003=9.3%, 2004=11.7%, 2005=12.6%, 2006=35.7%, 2007=23.1%, 2008=21.0%, 2009=10.1%, 2010=8.4%, 2011=8.1%, 2012=7.7%, 2013=6.9%, 2014=6.5%, 2015=12.6%, 2016=17.3%, 2017=14.6%, 2018=9.8%, 2019=11.7%, 2020=10.5%, 2021=11.8%, 2022=8.7%, 2023=6.1%, 2024=16.2%, 2025=9.0%, 2026=71.9%
- AND FY2026 IS NOT MERELY HIGH - IT IS AN 8x OUTLIER ON ITS OWN PANEL (9.0% in FY2025 against 71.9%). FAR practice is the standing rule and does not change year to year, so the rule alone does NOT explain this. The leading candidate is the VINTAGE: a partial year captured mid-flight holds the modifications to existing awards without yet holding the new awards those modifications will eventually sit under. That makes FY2026 a PIPELINE fact on top of a REGIME one, and it is the reason FY2026 counts must not be published at all - not merely caveated.
- **A CONTRACT-COUNT TREND RUNNING INTO THE RECENT YEARS IS AN ARTEFACT OF REPORTING PRACTICE.** Count AWARDS on a de-duplicated PIID key, or report dollars. Note this compounds with SANITY-04 in docs/CICD_BENCHMARK.md, where no Cedar award key reproduces CICD's 50,167 contracts: the grain question and the micro-modification question are the same question asked twice.

### The two that most endanger the editorial slate

1. **`HLOGA_QUARTERLY` (2008).** LDA filings went semiannual → quarterly. Filing COUNTS roughly double with no change in lobbying activity. Cedar's lobbying series runs 1999–2026, so **every filing-count trend in it crosses this break.** The registrant-concentration series (top-5 share 35.9% in 1999 → 24.6% in 2024) crosses it, and a concentration share computed on filings is a share of a denominator that doubled mid-series. Recompute on DOLLARS, or on filings-per-reporting-period, before publishing any of it.
2. **`COVID_RELIEF` (2020–21).** CARES and ARPA sent reportedly ~$8B and ~$20B directly to tribal governments. **Any 2020–2021 assistance spike is presumptively REGIME.** Note the trap in the row counts: assistance calendar-year counts move 46,112 → 49,660 → 52,321 across 2020–22, which is a mild trend and looks like nothing. **The money does not have to move the way the row counts move** — a relief programme can be a small number of very large transactions. Check the dollars, per CFDA, before typing any of it.

## KNOWN FALSE ATTRIBUTIONS — re-tested every run

*A spike sitting on a known-bad link is a PIPELINE fact, not a world fact. These run as regressions so that a fix that silently reverts is caught by the next sweep.*

**Why it was live for twenty days.** `65_lobbying_organization_type_guard.py` withdrew SALT RIVER PROJECT — an Arizona public power and irrigation district — from `native_entity_lobbying_disclosures.csv` at **2026-08-06 16:19**. The panel had been built at **2026-08-05 17:28** and was never rebuilt. The correction was applied. It was applied to one file. **A correction that is not applied to the table that PUBLISHES is not a correction, it is a note** — the same sentence `AGENTS.md` already carried about rulings, arriving by a different road.

**The second, undocumented instance is also cleared.** `350_withdraw_false_lobbying_attributions.py` withdrew **471 filings / $5,756,834** across 18 clients the name-form guard could not see, every one demonstrably a different organisation: Santa Rosa County FLORIDA (149 filings), Santa Rosa Junior College (25), Santa Rosa Memorial and CHRISTUS Santa Rosa hospitals (24), Team Santa Rosa EDC (22), COEUR D'ALENE **MINING** (8 — the guard bars `MINES` and this is the same firm spelled `MINING`), Bristol Bay Economic Development Corporation (135), Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation (99), and two Bristol Bay fishermen's associations (9). None has a spine entity, so all are UNLINKED, never repointed and never tier-X. `matched_alias`, `attribution_method`, `client_name` and every dollar column are preserved on the row; four `attribution_withdrawn_*` columns carry the refusal and its verbatim reason.

**The publishable slice is unchanged.** All 471 were `medium`. `high` still reads **23,741 filings / $627,601,108**, so the number `docs/EDITORIAL_PIPELINE.md` names for publication did not move. Attributed spend across all tiers is now **$680,041,390.52**.

### `FA-02` — FOIA index entity links · **CORRECTED 2026-08-26**

`data/clean/foia_request_index.csv` · corrected in place by `code/352_unlink_false_foia_entity_links.py`

- **rows**: 9,481 (unchanged — an unlink keeps the row)
- **linked_rows**: 453 → **344**
- **`AKNF-GEORGT-00-CALSTA-ASVCPR`**: 94 → **0**
- **`TRBF-ENTPRS-00`**: 17 → **2**
- **top_linked_entities now**: `TRBF-COQLLE-00` 55 · `TRBF-SNCNAT-00` 9 · `TRBF-UKEETW-00` 8 · `TRBF-MNACAN-00` 8 · `TRBF-SHNNCK-00` 7 · `AKNF-MTLKTL-00-TLNGHD` 7

**What the 94 actually were.** 92 matched inside a list of EMAIL DOMAINS a requester asked the agency to search — *"'wcl.american.edu' OR 'cpl.ucla.edu' OR 'ucla.edu' OR **'georgetown.edu'** OR 'law.georgetown.edu' OR 'stanford.edu'"*. The other 2 matched **Georgetown Climate Center**, a Washington DC policy centre listed beside Earthjustice and the Sierra Club. **No row anywhere in the file contains "Native Village of Georgetown."**

**What the 15 withdrawn Enterprise rows were:** `Solutions for Enterprise-Wide Procurement (SEWP) V` (×3), `D--JTM ENTERPRISE ZOOM LICENSES` (×2), the **American** Enterprise Institute, the **Competitive** Enterprise Institute, `Enterprise Security and Assessment Support Services`, an `Enterprise Data Inventory`, `Bing Chat Enterprise`, `Enterprise Human Resources Integration (EHRI)`, the `Superfund Enterprise Management System`, a contractor named `Elite Enterprise`, the phrase "Criminal Enterprise", and an obituary on `examiner-enterprise`.

**Two Enterprise rows were KEPT, and the asymmetry is deliberate.** `DOI-2025-001151` carries the full name *"Enterprise Rancheria of Maidu Indians of California"* — CONFIRMED, and the audit now says so. `DOI-2025-001646` is an AS-IA land-to-trust decision-letter request whose parsed description **truncates** at *"...by the Enterprise"*; it is not demonstrably wrong, so it stays at tier B with the truncation named. **An unlink needs evidence exactly as much as a link does.**

**Why demotion was not enough, and why not tier X.** The prior pass wrote *"Link retained, demoted, staged for a ruling"* on all 166 disputed rows. A demoted wrong link is still a wrong link in a column called `tribe_entity_id`, and every consumer of that column reads a link, not a caveat. Tier X was refused because `169_build_identifier_graph.py` treats X as a statement about the IDENTIFIER: blacklisting `TRBF-ENTPRS-00` would suppress the two rows in this same file that genuinely are Enterprise Rancheria. **The identifier is sound; 109 specific links were not.**

**PROVENANCE PRESERVED, on purpose.** `tribe_mentioned` and `tribe_match_phrase` are untouched, the withdrawn id is kept in a new `tribe_entity_id_withdrawn`, and `tribe_entity_link_audit` now reads `UNLINKED_FALSE_MATCH (...): <reason> EVIDENCE: "<verbatim window>" ... PRIOR AUDIT: <the whole earlier DISPUTED text>`. A correction has to be visible and reversible, not erased.

**STILL OPEN, named:** **55 rows remain `DISPUTED_FREE_TEXT_SINGLE_TOKEN` at tier B** — Shinnecock 7, Metlakatla 7, Ewiiaapaayp 7, Chickaloon 6, Muckleshoot 5, Seminole Tribe of Florida 5, Narragansett 5, Miccosukee 3, Passamaquoddy 2, Shoalwater 2, and one each of Snoqualmie, Bridgeport, Petersburg, Qawalangin, Winnemucca and Omaha Tribe of Nebraska. **These were not touched and should not be swept.** Unlike `georgetown` and `Enterprise`, these are distinctive tribal names appearing in FOIA prose about those tribes, and a request *about* the Shinnecock is plausibly a `SUBJECT_OF_REQUEST` link. They need reading, one at a time, not a rule.

### `FA-03` — TRBF-ENTPRS-00 canonical name is literally 'Enterprise' · **STANDING CAUTION**

A canonical name that is a common English noun attracts name-matched rows from every source. Entity-spike rows in this report carrying this id are typed PIPELINE by the classifier for that reason.

**Confirmed and quantified 2026-08-26.** The `foia_request_index` instance was corrected (see FA-02), but the caution is not retired and must not be: `prime_contracts.csv` carries **306** rows and `prime_contracts_archive_backfill.csv` **244** rows in which the string `Enterprise` appears alongside `TRBF-ENTPRS-00`, `nagpra_notice_entity_bridge.csv` **27**, `gaming_ordinances.csv` **3**. Those were NOT audited row-by-row here and most are presumably the real Enterprise Rancheria. The point stands: **this id cannot be checked by a token test**, in either direction. Any sweep that keys on it needs the surrounding text read.

### `FA-04` — Bristol Bay Area Health Corporation attributed to Bristol Bay Native Corporation · **LIVE, NEW 2026-08-26, NOT FIXED**

*Found by `354_correction_register.py`'s propagation check on its first run, while discharging FA-01. It is the largest false attribution this project has measured and it is deliberately NOT fixed in that session — see "why not fixed here".*

**The root, one row.** `data/clean/cedar_identifier_ledger_final.csv`:

| | |
|---|---|
| `identifier_type` / `identifier` | UEI · **`NL5HNWNUFMK4`** |
| `legal_business_name` | **BRISTOL BAY AREA HEALTH CORPORATION** |
| `tribe_id` / `canonical_name` | **`ANRC-BRBYCO-00`** · Bristol Bay Native Corporation |
| `attribution_method` | `cluster_v3` |
| `confidence_tier` / `tier_rationale` | **B** · *"Algorithmic name clustering, unreviewed"* |

BBAHC (EIN 920044965, Dillingham AK) is a **tribal health organisation**. BBNC is the **ANCSA regional corporation**. They are different entities, and `data/spine/cedar_entity_spine.csv` holds no entry for BBAHC — which is why the ledger's clusterer reached for the nearest name.

**What inherited it, measured 2026-08-26:**

| table | rows | quantity |
|---|---:|---|
| `federal_funding_transactions.csv` | **504** | **$494,305,407** obligated, `attribution_method = uei_exact_archive` |
| `cedar_identifier_graph_nodes.csv` | 2 | UEI node: 676 rows / **$776,715,576** observed; DUNS `081488264`: 15 rows / $26.6M |
| `subawards.csv` | 29 | `sub_native_tribe_id` |
| `fac_tribal_single_audits.csv` | 4 | FY2023–25 Single Audits, $53.8M / $60.0M / $67.4M expended |
| `np_schedule_i_grants.csv` | 4 | `cedar_recipient_spine_entity_id` |
| `native_passthrough.csv` | 4 | ~$323k of tribe-to-tribe passthrough labelled BBNC |
| `cedar_identifier_ledger_tiered.csv` / `cedar_identifier_propagation.csv` | 1 each | the propagation row is `publishable: NO`, tier B |

**A second, unexamined instance sits beside it:** 50 more `federal_funding_transactions` rows key **`BRISTOL BAY HOUSING AUTHORITY`** to `ANRC-BRBYCO-00`. Together with the 504, **every assistance row attributed to BBNC is attributed to an organisation that is not BBNC.** The housing authority was not audited and is not counted in the ten.

**Why it is not fixed here.** Unlinking 504 rows moves **`village_corp_obligations_usd`**, which `62_no_regression_check.py` holds as MUST_NOT_FALL at **$60,402,736,070**. That is the gate working: a half-billion dollars leaving an attribution column is exactly what it is built to stop, and clearing it needs an owner's ruling on whether BBAHC (and BBHA) become spine entities, not a drive-by edit. Tier B "never publishes alone", which bounds the damage but does not remove it — `federal_funding_transactions.tribe_id` is a shipping column.

**How to discharge it.** (1) Rule on BBAHC and BBHA as spine entities — both are real Native organisations with their own EINs, so this is a REPOINT, not an unlink. (2) Correct the ledger row on `NL5HNWNUFMK4`. (3) Re-run `169_build_identifier_graph.py`. (4) Declare each correction via `354_correction_register.py` so the ten stale consumers re-test to zero. `62`'s `corrections_not_propagated` carries the floor of **10** until then, and prints all ten by name on every run.

## THE FORBIDDEN SUMS — columns present in these files that must never be totalled

*Recorded so a phantom is recognisable by its magnitude. Every one of these produces a plausible-looking number, which is worse than an obviously wrong one.*

**`prime_contracts`** (`prime_contracts.csv`, mtime 2026-08-26T18:45:37)

- `total_award_value` — award ceiling restated on every transaction of the award (MAX_PER_AWARD_COLUMNS)
- `total_obligations_real2025` — deflated restatement of total_obligations; sums to $385.0B against a true $310.01B
- `total_award_value_real2025` — restatement of a column that is already a restatement
- `deflator_factor_2025` — an index, not a quantity

**`federal_funding_transactions`** (`federal_funding_transactions.csv`, mtime 2026-08-26T18:12:57)

- `face_value_of_loan` — not an obligation
- `original_loan_subsidy_cost` — not an obligation
- `total_face_value_of_loan` — award-cumulative and signed; face value is the borrower's principal, not federal outlay
- `total_loan_subsidy_cost` — a different quantity from an obligation; never added to one
- `obligated_usd_real2025` — deflated restatement of obligated_usd
- `deflator_factor_2025` — an index, not a quantity

**`subawards`** (`subawards.csv`, mtime 2026-08-26T18:58:58)

- `prime_award_amount` — the prime award's value restated on every subaward row of that prime
- `subaward_amount_real2025` — deflated restatement of subaward_amount
- `deflator_factor_2025` — an index, not a quantity

**`nagpra_notices`** (`nagpra_notices.csv`, mtime 2026-08-06T19:01:12)

- `mni_total_stated` — A COUNT OF HUMAN BEINGS. Never summed, never averaged, never charted as a volume.

**`deals_classified`** (`deals_classified.csv`, mtime 2026-08-26T17:15:02)

- `Project_Total_Value_USD` — project total restated across rows of the same project

**`resource_revenue`** (`resource_revenue.csv`, mtime 2026-08-12T20:52:08)

- `deflator_factor_2025` — an index, not a quantity

## How to re-run this, and how to read a row

    py -3 code/227_anomaly_sweep.py
    py -3 code/227_anomaly_sweep.py --only prime_contracts,subawards

**Read-only against every dataset.** Zero network calls. Writes `docs/ANOMALY_REPORT.md` and `docs/anomaly_report.json` and nothing else. Never runs `01_build_entity_spine.py`, `09_import_rulings.py`, `41_build_codebooks.py` or `88_build_deals_taxonomy.py`.

Four rules for handling a row:

1. **Do not close an UNKNOWN by finding a story.** A definitional or regime explanation is admissible only if it NAMES the change and the named change is checkable in the data. "Probably a coverage thing" is not an explanation; it is the absence of one wearing its clothes.
2. **Do not widen a threshold to make a row disappear.** This file records anomalies, not tolerances. A sweep that is always clean reports nothing — the same decoration failure `AGENTS.md` records against `62_no_regression_check.py`.
3. **A `REGIME` row is not a defect and must not be fixed.** It is a caveat that has to travel with every sentence built on that series. Fix the sentence, not the data.
4. **A `PIPELINE` row has an owning script named in its evidence.** An unnamed failure gets inherited; a named one gets fixed.

### What this sweep does NOT do

- **A seam does not have to fall on a date.** Every test here except `SOURCE_VOCABULARY_SPLIT` compares adjacent years, and two pulls that OVERLAP in time mix their vocabularies inside every year where no year boundary can separate them. `prime_contracts.funding_agency` is the worked example and it is why that one test exists. It runs only where the dataset spec names an `era_col`.
- It compares **adjacent years**. A slow drift over a decade — a linkage rate creeping up as passes land — never trips a year-over-year test and is invisible here.
- It types a year, not a transaction. A REGIME window covering 2020–21 will type an ordinary 2020 spike as REGIME. **That is deliberate and it is the conservative direction**: it costs a true finding, and the opposite error ships a false one.
- Its categorical seam detector picks candidate columns from the first 120,000 rows and drops any column exceeding 350 distinct values there. **A seam in a high-cardinality column is invisible to it.**
- Every anomaly carries a CONTENT-ADDRESSED `anomaly_id` (md5 over dataset + class + column + entity + year). It is deliberately NOT positional and deliberately not built on Python's `hash()`, which is randomised per process — three ids elsewhere in this repo are built that way and a re-run changed 482 of 492 of them. An id that moves when nothing moved makes a diffable artefact undiffable.
- Benford and round-number clustering are **prompts to look, never findings**. Federal money is full of legitimate reasons to fail both.
